newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil subdued, but steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil subdued, but steady.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil markets were subdued on Friday with limited demand weighing on attempts to move a number of cargoes, traders said.
Sellers, eyeing the fluctuations in crude, were for now resisting attempts to push prices further down, they added.
One small packet of low sulphur straight-run was sold inland Europe at $97 fob, while prices for larger cargoes of 0.6 percent material were heard steady at around $93/$95 fob.
The week's U.S. buying interest for specific quality grades was reported still present, with one fixture lined up by Sun for April 19 loading to take British material trans-atlantic.
Russian residual fuel vessels were on offer, but attracting much less interest than pre-Easter, with refiners preferring the more lucrative processing of crude.
"People are having to come down to get rid of things," said one trader.
However, a large trading firm was heard to have sold an E-4 aboard the Moskovsky Festival, loading April 18-19, for a healthy three means plus $3 to a French major.
Traders said the going rate for E-4 was three means flat, with Thursday's trade, the Talava, done for $90 cif.
